description: The red cluster belongs also to the “socioeconomics” category and is named accordingly. The “socioeconomics” cluster is composed of four streams. The first one is “Introductory”, albeit focusing on derivative applications that have emerged from the core DeFi domain. Lee (2023) proposes NFTs as decentralized alternative to the current obsolete intellectual property protection and copyright system. Proelss et al. (2023) introduces us to “GameFi”, as a symbiosis between Gaming, NFTs and DeFi. Burger & Weinmann (2022) analyzes why the energy sector couldn’t leverage the blockchain technology as the financial sector did. The second stream (new in this analysis) is formed by systematic literature review articles: Puschmann & Huang-Sui (2024) develops a taxonomy, Gramlich et al., (2023) present multivocal literature review, Eikmanns et al. (2023) provide a conceptualization and outlook for Decentralized Finance. Bennett et al. (2023) utilizes a systematic literature review with the lenses of Behavioral finance theory. Grassi et al. (2022) review secondary data to evaluate the need for financial intermediation based on “information asymmetry” and “transaction costs” concepts. The third stream is called “market failure”. In it we find Barbereau et al. (2023) which arrive to the conclusion that in Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs) “minority rule” and not an inclusive democratic as originally intended, this concentration risk was labeled “fake-DeFi” while Saengchote (2023) found that the top 100 addresses manage roughly 80% of the lending and borrowing in the “Compound” DeFi protocol signaling a high degree of centralization, which contradicts the protocol's core tenet of decentralization. Bhambhwani & Huang, (2024) describe possible types of protocol exploits and how auditing smart contracts can enhance protocol value by providing assurance regarding the safety of user’s funds. This cluster seems to continue the tacit discussion regarding the need for regulation. The three mentioned papers within the “market failure” understand that applying regulation is challenging to implement in DeFi (and they refrain from recommending it). While Bhambhwani & Huang, (2024) conclusion implies that DeFi, because of its open-source nature, might improve itself with its own mechanisms. Lee (2023) explicitly relies on the “code as law” principle operating as a private ordering, akin to private regulation. The fourth and last stream in this category is “tokenomics”, with documents evaluating crypto assets adoption and return based on user generated content and other non-financial metrics. Nguyen & Nguyen (2024) focuses on the social, economic, and cultural factors influencing DeFi adoption. Piñeiro-Chousa et al. (2022) wrote an initial article about how DeFi cryptocurrencies are affected by other financial assets like gold and oil as well as user content. Later, Piñeiro-Chousa et al., (2023) based their impact analysis mainly in “social metrics” like change in amount of tweet posts or the weekly change in the number of likes on relevant social posts.

the blue cluster is the “technological”, tightly related to the computer science field. And its first stream is also security (Trozze et al., 2023; Cui & Gao, 2023; W. Li et al., 2022; Mazorra et al., 2022). The second stream is focused on technological improvements to the blockchain in response to second generation challenges. Joshi et al., (2023), Buldas et al. (2022) and Westerkamp & Küpper (2023) present quantum computers based blockchain, scalable blockchain and cross blockchain smart contracts respectively.

the green cluster is formed by financial articles. Articles in this cluster focus on the relationship between NFTs, DeFi tokens, cryptocurrencies within themselves or compared against traditional asset’s indexes. The relationship is generally measured by volatility spillovers and returns. Comparisons are interested in the effects of global crisis like Covid-19 pandemic or the Russia-Ukraine war. There are comparisons to specific markets like Abakah et al., (2023) interested in the relationship with eco-friendly assets or Fakhfekh et al., (2024) with gold backed crypto-assets. Alon et al. (2023) applies machine learning to predict NFT prices. Mensi et al. (2024) analyze the connectedness between major cryptocurrencies and nonfungible tokens.
